### J-9485 2026-11-18 M2-FIX archive validation deletes no segment (PM ruling 10) - defect
Evidence: `AH/archive/store.js` `observeNow`, `scanSegments`, `sealNow`; `AH/archive/segment.js`
`writeSegment`; commit 77585802a7; tests `test/adapter/m2-archive-store.test.js` "J-9485 (B)",
"J-9485 (A)", "J-9485: a segment file that cannot be read", the rewritten "validation" test, and
`m2-archive-kill.test.js` (18 tests, about 24 s wall, Node, no supervisor); integration
`m2-archive-restart-2` passed in a shared slot (209 s) and `m2-archive-restart` (153 s, S
and A3 kills) at 781c2f3bf0; the whole unit and adapter lane: 727 passed, 0 failed, 65 s wall.
Reading: M2-R2's J-9445 is fixed in store.js only. (1) No code path outside session delete
(`release`) unlinks a final-named segment: validation keeps every file of the vat's chain, every
file the manifest records `acknowledged`, and every file that chains forward from the vat's state
(any branch, any length: a seal answered in this or an earlier incarnation whose crank Z has not
run); an orphan is only a file at an ordinal the vat's chain already fixes with another digest, and
it is renamed `<name>.orphan` (out of scans, its blob keys still counted live, removed with the
session). `sealNow` sets replaced entries aside the same way and refuses (never deletes) if one is
acknowledged. (2) Staleness comes from the persisted acknowledged chain: a state that is a proper
prefix of the manifest's acknowledged entries changes nothing; with no state in memory the
acknowledged prefix becomes the validated state after its files are stat'ed. So LRU eviction (B)
and a restart (A) no longer matter, and the J-0493 (3) delivery-order assumption carries nothing.
(3) `scanSegments` keeps a file that does not verify (counted `unreadable`) and throws on a read
error with an errno (EACCES in the test stands for EIO/EMFILE); `writeSegment` keeps a damaged file
of the same name as `<name>.bad` before writing the verified one. The two reviewer scenarios are
tests now: (B) `maxSessions: 1`, two segments acknowledged, the state evicted by another session,
the pre-seal page observed: both files kept, the next prepare equals the oracle; (A) incarnation 1
answers, incarnation 2 observes the older state, then Z: kept, acknowledged, equal to the oracle.
Behaviour change: an answered seal the vat never applied now stays on disk until the vat seals that
ordinal again (the same range reuses the file; another range sets it aside), at most one file per
crash; the kill tests now assert "acknowledged plus at most the unapplied answer", and only the
chain after the next seal.
Fit: awkward, and now explicit: an orthogonally persistent vat keeps the acknowledged chain for
free, while the Node adapter must persist the fact (manifest flags) before it can act on it;
deciding deletion from adapter memory was the defect. Good: chained digests make "is this a
prefix of what the vat named" a constant-time check.
Decision: done; contract 4.2, 4.5 and 4.7 restated (deletion follows only from the persisted
chain).

### J-9486 2026-11-18 M2-FIX security review fixes (M2-R1) - defect
Evidence: commits 7fb0d89457 (providers) and 3c111fc57a (secrets); tests

`https:` or `http:` to localhost/127.0.0.1/[::1], or has user info, a query or a fragment, with a
fixed text, in the OpenRouter and Anthropic providers and the catalogue; (c) a round's whole

fails with `texts.frameLimit` and the body is cancelled (test: 69.2 MB streamed before the cut,

### J-9491 2026-11-18 M2-FIX PM rulings 5 and 9: where the specification wins - decision
Evidence: SPEC R6-44, R4-47, R4-83, A.4 `getUsage` and the `usage` event (read in the
specification, not from memory of the reference); commit 8c538130dd; contract 5.1 and decision 12;
`test/unit/m2-queue-submissions.test.js` (17 pass), `test/integration/m2-queue.test.js`
(passed, 180 s, shared slot, at 781c2f3bf0).
Reading: (a) R6-44 states that Send now "for the queue head cancels the running turn so it goes
next": built. `QueueEntry.sendNow` moves the entry to the head, releases holds, claims when idle;
when a turn runs and no hold is left it cancels that turn (`runner.cancelCurrent`, as
`Turn.cancel()`), and the entry is claimed when the cancelled turn settles. The old unit test that
asserted "a running turn is never cut short" now asserts the cut. (b) Usage `turns`: R4-83, A.4
and the event say "turns, incomplete turns" only; silent on which turns count, so the contract
(every settled turn) stands. (c) The R4-47 round-limit text: the specification says only that the
turn "ends normally with" it; silent on later contexts, so the contract (`TurnSettled.final`, not a
transcript record) stands. Session bundle 186,611 -> 187,018 bytes.
Decision: applied.

### J-9492 2026-11-18 M2-FIX PM ruling 6: receipts bounded by eviction - decision
Evidence: commit 668f054b80 (its subject says 187,173; the bundle measured 187,284 bytes after it,
from 187,018); `guest/lib/pending-queue.js` (12 lines of vat code); `test/unit/m1a-queue.test.js`,
`m2-queue-pending.test.js` (63 queue tests pass).
Reading: R4-98 says "4096 receipts kept" and R4-53 that the queue bounds what is held. A full
table no longer refuses: the oldest inserted receipt is evicted, and the session keeps one number,
the latest issue time evicted; an unknown id issued at or before it is refused with
`texts.requestIdExpired`, so a retry whose receipt was evicted is never run twice. Retained state:
4,096 receipts plus one number. Cost: a client whose clock lags can see a fresh id refused as
expired while the table turns over within its lag.
Decision: applied; contract 5.1 restated.

### J-9494 2026-11-18 M2-FIX checkpoint.stall: the cause is the core's cadence snapshot - perf
Evidence: J-9462's per-turn split (engine snapshot count and time per turn, at 200, 1,000 and
5,000 turns); `packages/thixotrope/src/core/durable-worker-transport.js` (the cadence check after
each delivery batch), `src/control/supervisor.js` (`snapshotEveryDeliveries = 256`),
`scripts/serve.mjs` (`--snapshot-every`); J-9463 (snapshot 34.4 MB, flat with length). No new run:
the earlier split already holds per-phase timing, and the code path explains it.
Reading: after every delivery batch the worker transport queues a snapshot once 256 deliveries have
passed since the last one, whether or not a turn is in progress; the snapshot runs behind the
queued deliveries and holds the next ones for its whole duration (0.7-5.2 s for the session vat's
34 MB heap under load). A turn of about 9 deliveries meets one every 28 turns, so every 100-turn
window holds 2-4, and p99 of 100 samples is that turn. It is not a seal crank (no slow turn sealed)
and nothing in harness code does the work in one turn, so no harness change spreads it. Raising
`--snapshot-every` would only make a window miss it (a measurement artefact, longer replay).
Fix size (core candidate): let the cadence defer a due snapshot until the worker has been idle for
a short time (for example 50 ms with no delivery queued), forced at 4 x the cadence: about 30 lines
in `durable-worker-transport.js` plus a test; or shrink the session heap (SES baseline and bundle;
a separate study).
Fit: poor fit as configured: orthogonal persistence pays its checkpoint on the turn path of
whichever turn crosses the count; a busy interactive vat wants checkpoints at idle.
Decision: budget unchanged; core candidate for the PM.

### J-9498 2026-11-18 M2 close-out fit: what the exclusive numbers say about Thixotrope - fit

Evidence: J-9495..J-9497; the shared-slot runs of M2-P1 and M2-P2 (J-9460..J-9473) for the same
files.
Reading: good fit: orthogonal persistence plus the record archive gives a session whose every
vat-side cost is independent of its length (5,000 against 200 turns at 0.95-1.07 x), restarts
with 50 sleeping 300-turn sessions serve in under 4.2 s and wake none, and on a quiet machine the
whole perf pass of 25 files fits in 70 minutes with no file over 5 minutes. Poor fit, measured:
(a) a busy vat pays its checkpoint inside whichever turn crosses the delivery count (C-24); (b)
the hub's per-row cost grows with sessions and viewers, not turns (C-2's rest), which is where
`concurrency.10` and `hub.growth` miss; (c) import is the only way to build long states and costs
what live turns cost per record (C-22): the template chain is the longest step of a pass (32
minutes of wall here). Load sensitivity is itself a finding: the same files held 1.3-2.2 x longer
in shared slots at load 4-7 than here, and some latency rows (exec.trivial 160 x, turn.start p99)
move far more than load explains, because every crank's host work runs on the supervisor's one
thread.
Decision: none beyond the candidates already filed.

### J-0552 2026-11-18 M3 W3.3 kit sameness - awkward
Evidence: `durable.js` registers with `same: () => true` and no `replaces`;
`pkg/src/native/manager-kit.js` `register` (an existing key whose spec is "same" is reconciled
with its old spec).
Reading: under the agent-host manager's sameness rule a second `register(GATEWAY_KEY, newSpec)`
would keep the old config silently. `serve` therefore closes the old registration (the adapter
unbinds, closing the listener) and registers anew, so a re-serve has a short window with no
listener and costs two kit operations. A per-key `same`/`replaces` would let the kit rebind under a
new epoch in one step; the kit takes one rule per manager.
Decision: close-then-register, as the contract states; admin operations are serialised in the
manager so a `status` between the two steps sees the whole change.

### J-0540 2026-11-18 M3 W3.2 CapTP bridge and guards - built
Evidence: e5b5a6c5c0, 2dd747655b: `AH/gateway/{bridge,guard,powers,vocabulary,extensions}.js`,
`test/adapter/m3-w32-{bridge,vocabulary,extensions,wire}.test.js` (27 tests, about 1.5 s, no
supervisor), `test/adapter/_m3-captp-client.js`, `test/fixtures/gateway-extension/`.
Reading: one captp connection per socket; the bridge parses every frame and checks each
`CTP_CALL` on its capdata form before `dispatch`. Rule 1 needs the exact export table, and
captp's `exportHook` sees exports but not their release, so the bridge passes captp its own
default tables through the `makeCapTPImportExportTables` option and observes `markAsExported`
and `deleteExport` (exact slot-to-value map and count; the 4,096 cap closes 4008 without sending
the over-limit answer). Answers are mirrored by the page's question ids; a refused question is
never an answer, so pipelining on it is refused too. Before sign-in only `CTP_BOOTSTRAP` and a
`fetch` on the bootstrap pass; sign-in is detected from the `CTP_RETURN` result of a `fetch`
question, so the bootstrap needs no callback. Calls in flight are question ids of forwarded calls
to non-local targets, released when captp sends their `CTP_RETURN`. Gateway-local objects are a
process-wide `WeakSet` in `powers.js` (bootstrap, Live facade and its wrapped subscriptions,
content, composer, history, extras, every LargeCall target): the CC-050 workaround as stated,
costing one `WeakSet` lookup per call.
Decision: as built; W3.7 wires `makeBridge` with `isLargeCall` from `makeLargeCalls`.

### J-9603 2026-11-18 M3 W3.8 Playwright and hardened promises in one process - fit
Evidence: the first browser run: `TypeError: Cannot add property Symbol(async_id_symbol), object
is not extensible` from the control client's `call` (`local-control.js:158`) after Chromium was
launched; probes without the supervisor did not reproduce it.
Reading: poor fit. Playwright's zones use `AsyncLocalStorage`, which on Node 22 turns on async
hooks; Node then tags each promise it tracks with an async id the first time it sees it, and a
promise hardened before the hooks were on (the control client's, made by `startFromTemplate`)
cannot take the symbol. Decision: `startBrowserGateway` launches Chromium before it starts
anything, which fixed it. A test that hardens promises before calling it (module-level
`harden(promise)`) can still hit it.

### J-9670 2026-11-18 M4 review fixes (M4-FIX) - build
Fixed from J-9661/J-9662: (1) retirement: the pool bridge asks `poolState` again when its answer
is older than `poolStateRefreshMs` (30 s; a retired answer is final, a failed ask keeps the old
one), so a retired pool fails and a retired member drops out within 30 s, at a cost of one
manager crank per used pool per 30 s and none while idle (not the contract's "next turn": that
needs a push, which the `CredentialOps` guard does not allow; asked of the PM). (2) Sign-in uses an
independent random OAuth `state`; the PKCE verifier no longer appears in the URL. (3)+(7) After
the refresh POST no rotated refresh token is dropped: a lifetime within the skew is written and
served; an answer refused later (token type, lifetime, `exp` past) is written back with the access
token marked spent; an answer naming another account still keeps nothing. (4) Usage reads are
single flight per member; the model's `accountStatus {refresh:true}` reads a member at most once
per 60 s (operator `Accounts.refresh` stays on demand). (6) Dated marks are capped at now + 8 days.
Tests: one new or strengthened adapter test per fix; M4 unit and adapter files 150 tests pass in
8.6 s. Fit: the manager deciding and the adapter caching per incarnation is cheap but leaves no
channel for the vat to tell the adapter; a push needs an interface the contract did not foresee.

240,000, exec 120,000), but the session program is 32,126 bytes over it and 9,982 over the
factory's hard cap (`maxProgramBytes` = `execSourceBytes` = 262,144): no session can be created
in this lane ("A session program is at most 262144 bytes in this build"). The contract estimated
+25 KB for M5; it is +85.7 KB: 13 new session modules (about 59 KB of code without comments),
about 1.3 KB of compartment-mapper scaffolding per module (48 KB in all, 37 modules), and the
edits to `turn.js`, `session.js`, `tool-table.js`. Leading indentation is 35,911 bytes of the

numbers J-0303 kept. The patch is the PM's to apply (`scripts/bundle-guest.mjs` is not an M5
file); every daemon run of W5.9 used a copy of the lane with it applied.
Fit: poor for this engine's staging model: the program is one source evaluated in a fresh vat,
so per-module scaffolding and indentation are paid in every session vat's staging (D-4, about

### J-9693 2026-11-18 A vat that sends a deeply nested record halts itself - fit

from the control client: the fixture in the workspace vat builds `parameters` 40 levels of

(the encoder should refuse a value too deep to send with an error, not halt the vat). Hostile
fixtures belong in a disposable vat.

pipelined on it is refused `notSignedIn`; only a table of unsettled answers closes (4008). Per
window, the questions a client held at once (asked, not yet dropped; an upper bound of the
gateway's table): ui.call 984 (1,372 calls), ui.submit 1,697 (355 samples, 3 calls each), ui.deltaFanout
1,746 on the main page and about 300 on each of the 4 others; bound 4,096, `boundHit` false in
every window. Server side (`gateway-connection-closed`): the main page answersPeak 1,746,
answersEvicted 0; 11,499 fetch connections peak 2; the probes connection (closed by its 4,097-export
probe, 4008) peaked at 4,096 with 12 evicted. Rows (under load): gateway.fetch median 0.73 ms,
gateway.guard 0.122 ms, ui.call 29.1 ms, ui.submit 66.1 ms, ui.deltaFanout median 1 ms; exit 1 is
the carried miss ui.deltaFanout 0.01 deliveries per delta (budget 0), not this unit.
Fit: poor margin: a Node client with `gcImports` drops its questions only when V8 collects them, so
a busy page holds about 1,000 questions a minute; 1,746 after three windows is 43 % of the bound.
A page running longer than about 4 busy minutes without a major GC will see evictions (it stays open;
only pipelining on an old answer is refused). A browser's GC cadence is not measured.

### J-10116 2026-11-18 CH which sessions and messages the ceiling bounds - decision
Evidence: `pkg/src/net/hub.js` `forwardToRow`, `handleMessage`, `settleToResolver`; `core/daemon.js`
`provideWorkerSession`; commit `0edc2ab05a`.
Reading: every message one session sends to another goes through `forwardToRow`; the check runs on
the frame re-encoded toward the destination, inside the forward's rollback scope, so a refused
message leaves no answer route or listener. Bounded: worker sessions only. Kinds: `op:deliver` with
an answer (answer and resolver break with `FRAME_TOO_LARGE`), deliver-only (dropped, logged),
`op:listen`, `op:get`/`op:index`/`op:untag`, and settlements toward the worker's own resolvers (the
answer to its call, a promise resolution): the resolver itself breaks, so the calling vat gets a
rejection. Not bounded: adapters, transient clients, endpoint, peers, and hub-made frames.
Decision: no persisted state (the option is given at every attach). Known gap: after a restart, a
frame toward a worker forwarded before that worker reattaches (only the endpoint is attached
earlier) is not bounded.

### J-10078 2026-11-18 K2 why serve time grows across SIGKILL restarts - measure
Evidence: core `daemon.js` startup sweep (every worker whose transport `owesDelivery()` is woken
before the daemon is handed out), `durable-worker-transport.js` `ensureAwake` (replay of the
journal from the snapshot cut) and `armCadenceTimer` (CC-026); `gateway-restart` exclusive at
`46cc84bb16`, idle sleep 1 h, cadence 256.
{"mode":"sigkill","restarts":24,"servedMs":[3939,3921,4169,4157,4651,4999,4727,5237,5325,6131,5845,6481,6507,7042,7007,7212,7879,7595,8370,8474,7931,7694,7984,8408],"owedReplayFrames":[52,99,158,220,274,320,366,411,458,504,560,605,652,709,757,802,849,906,959,1010,813,860,913,705]}
{"mode":"clean","restarts":30,"servedMs":"3245..3704","owedReplayFrames":"46..79"}
Before the last SIGKILL restart the owed frames were registry 184, workspace:default 185,
workspace:w 178, app:harness 72, native:agentHostAdmin 46, native:clock 32, native:control 8.
Reading: it is the journal replay. No vat sleeps (idle sleep 1 h) and a SIGKILL takes no
snapshot, so each restart's sign-in and connect add about 48 journal frames across the awake
workers, and the next start replays all of them before `serve()` resolves: 52 -> 1,010 frames
over 20 kills, serve 3.9 -> 8.5 s, about 4.7 ms of serve per owed frame. A clean stop snapshots,
so the clean series stays at 46-79 owed frames and 3.2-3.7 s. With CC-026 the growth is bounded:
a wake whose replay leaves a cadence (256) of entries snapshots once quiet, seen twice
(agentHostAdmin after 251, control after 255: the sum fell 1,010 -> 813 and 913 -> 705, serve
8.5 -> 7.9 s). The bound is per worker, so with seven awake workers the
replay can still reach about 7 x 256 frames. C-3 stands as recorded; the row passes because the
gateway answers before `serve()` resolves (median -1.9 s).
Fit: neutral: bounded by CC-026, not removed.

### J-0810 2026-11-18 W6.0 the M6 contract: one environments resource - decision
Evidence: `designs/m6-interfaces.md` (sections 2, 6, 8), `resources/environments/interfaces.js`
(51 guards and shapes built in Node with the guest prelude; every interface's method list equals
its guard's; no absent Git method on the writer; a settings record with an extra key refused);
`designs/arch-review/step3-plan.md` at `53a8dbb9ea` (read before fixing the session seams);
`resources/agent-host/durable.js` (attach pattern), `pkg/src/native/contract.js`, `pkg/src/control/supervisor.js`
`installNative` (no grants, no configuration), `packages/git/src/native-git-backend.js`
(`GIT_BASE_ARGS`, `EXECUTABLE_REPO_CONFIG`).
Reading: a container's `/workspace` is the workspace directory, so two resources would pass a host
path or a guessed key between processes; one resource keeps every identity in its manager and
finds a session's directory from the presence it was handed. Configuration travels in the service
key's spec, since `installNative` carries none (AR-SYN-28; CC-091 asked). Commands on the turn path
go through a per-incarnation `ShellPort` (vat -> adapter -> vat 70-76 ms) instead of the manager
(164-175 ms per call), and a break from it is the command's unknown outcome, not a restart: the
environments adapter can be rebuilt while the agent-host lease lives. The guard table sits beside
the resource: no harness vat program bundles it and no browser reaches it, and in `guest/lib/` it
would have to join or be excluded from the gateway vocabulary, which the vocabulary test refuses
for uncovered interfaces. Session seams (part `environment`, an `admit` hook, `Session` methods)
are designed against step 3 and marked provisional until it merges.
Decision: D-M6-1..D-M6-14 as written; work units W6.0b (shared guard entries, first and alone),
W6.1-W6.6 in parallel, W6.7 integration, W6.8 fold; core requests CC-090..CC-092.
Fit: good for identities and restart (lazy, one registration); awkward where the core has no
service shape or configuration (the attach and argv workarounds a second time).

### J-1431 2026-11-19 WX.1 the part and tool orders as slotted tables - decision
Evidence: `628a30884f`, `c7d4b0d9a3`.
Decision: `PartName` names all nine parts and `Runtime` the four to come (optional), so the lanes'
five-line R-1/S1/S-7 seams become four lines each, every one directly below its own
`// slot: <name>` comment (import, `requiredParts`, `runtimeParts`, getter); the tool table has a
slot per group (shell, `viewImage`, mail, requests, subagents). Lines of two lanes never touch, so
git merges them without conflict. No part and no tool registered; `requiredParts` gains a part in
the lane commit that adds it (a required part that does not exist yet would stop every session).

unchanged in behaviour, plus `held()`. The sentence split is incremental: each push scans only
the units it added (Endo's chunker rescanned its buffer per push and looked back with a regex
over everything before each period, quadratic on a long reply); the abbreviation and list-marker
checks look back a bounded number of units; a run of `sentenceUnits` with no boundary is cut at
its last whitespace, never inside a surrogate pair. `lineBreak()` starts a fresh code filter (an
unclosed fence in one message does not silence the next) and releases a chunk under 10 units
alone, so no sentence spans a tool call. The view reads `Live.subscribe(session)` in process,
compares a final with the round's text only (whitespace collapsed; a revised final adds
nothing), reads a staged final through `Content` a page at a time, treats every abort as the
end, ends on another turn's `turn-start` (a channel gap) and aborts `turnNotFound` when the
channel drops it. Views are counted per `Live` and per session in `WeakMap`s.
Fit: good. The channel's snapshot-then-deliveries contract is exactly what a speech view needs;
no session crank, no vat delivery.

### J-1332 2026-11-19 W11.1 contract gaps found while building - finding
Evidence: contract 6.2, 3.3, 5.2; `engine-types.js` `SttEngine`, `UtteranceSink`, `Utterance`.
Reading: (1) "Utterance `n` is engine stream `u<n>`" cannot hold: one engine serves every port of
the incarnation and each port numbers its first utterance 1, and `SttEngine.open(sink)` takes no
number; engine ids are `u<k>` from the engine's own wrapping counter. (2) `UtteranceSink` has no
way to carry the `utteranceTooLong` note of the `end` event; the utterance answers `tooLong()`
(type `ProcessUtterance`), which the route reads at the final. (3) The settings' `command` is used
as the whole argv; `language` is not appended (the provisioning default carries `--lang`).
(4) `engineTimeoutMs` would kill an engine still loading its model (600 s allowed), so its timer
runs only while the engine is ready. (5) With the real Moonshine, partials come only when the
text changes, so 11 s of continuous non-speech audio after a word would time the engine out; the
client's endpointing ends such an utterance first (1.2 s of silence), so this is left as written.
(6) Pacing holds a start for `backoffMs` without waiting: an utterance opened meanwhile aborts
`engineUnavailable` at once (the user is waiting).
Fit: neutral.

### J-12641 2026-11-19 W11.6 both sockets race for a stream's first frame - finding
Evidence: `audio-socket.js` at `ac6f288303`; `voice-audio-socket.test.js` "events before its
number are held".
Reading: a stream is opened by a CapTP call on `/ws` and its frames travel on `/audio`, and the
server sends `phase: listening` (or the first PCM) as soon as it opened the stream, so the
`/audio` frame can arrive before the CapTP answer that names it. The client holds frames of
unclaimed numbers (at most `streamsPerPort` numbers and `pcmBufferedBytes` in all, the oldest
number dropped first and its stream aborting with `speechTexts.backlog` when claimed) and queues
an utterance's audio until its number comes (at most `sttBacklogBytes`, then the utterance
aborts and only an ABORT goes out). Frames for a number the page has ended are dropped, not held.
The contract's section 4 does not state the race; W11.5's server needs nothing for it.
Fit: neutral (a cost of D-M11-3's two sockets, bounded on the client).

### J-12643 2026-11-19 W11.6 endpointing differs from Endo in two places - finding
Evidence: `endpointing.js` at `5a2adbb1ea`; `voice-endpointing.test.js`.
Reading: (1) Endo measures minimum speech from onset to the END decision, which includes the
1,200 ms trailing silence, so its 400 ms minimum never discards anything; here speech is the span
from the onset block to the last block above the threshold, so acceptance 6's 400 ms burst is
discarded (340 ms of loud block starts) and a 600 ms one is kept. (2) A discarded blip during the
grace window re-arms the pending text's send (`makeSpokenDraft().dropped`), where Endo left the
text in the box unsent. Barge-in follows Endo's code, not the defaults file's comment: the
barge-in threshold is max(minimum, speech threshold x 3), not floor x 3.

### J-1352 2026-11-19 W11.2 contract gaps found while building - finding
Evidence: contract 6.2, D-M11-12, 3.3; `engine-types.js` `TtsEngine`, `Synthesis`,
`PlaybackSink`; `AH/speech/host.js` (W11.5, uncommitted when read).
Reading: (1) Piper's raw output has no sentence boundary, so "a sentence with no PCM within
`synthTimeoutMs`" needs a known start per sentence: sentences are written in lock step (the next
at the previous one's first PCM), which keeps the pipelining (Piper writes a sentence's audio
after synthesizing it) and gives each written sentence a start. With paused output the tail of
sentence k can arrive after k+1 was written and credit k+1 early, so a reported failed index can
be one later than the sentence that hung, never earlier. (2) `TtsEngine` has no way to learn the
shared preferences, so the warm spare follows the latest playback's options (at first the
catalogue defaults) and `warm(options?)` is an extra method (type `ProcessTtsEngine`) the host
may call with `Voice.getPreferences()`; a playback with other options drops the spare. (3) There
is no fixed text for "the default voice is unusable": the warning joins `unknownVoice(id)` (or
`outOfRange('speed', ...)`) and `speechOutOff`. (4) A process that keeps failing is bounded per
playback (two failed sentences in a row abort `synthFailed`), not by `engineRestart` pacing,
which is a rate across utterances of a resident engine. (5) `fake-tts.mjs`'s `hang-on=<index>`
counts sentences across every process logging to the same `--log` file, so it names one sentence
of a playback even across a respawn. (6) `host.js` carries its own `checkTtsOptions`; the
contract puts it in `voice-catalogue.js`.
Fit: neutral.

### J-12623 2026-11-19 W11.5 contract differences and a pinned list - finding
Evidence: `69fa32328c`, `c4cf4d6dc3`; `test:integration m3-gateway` 107.8 s held.
Reading: (1) `makeSpeechHost` takes a fourth input, `pipeline: { openTurnView, makeSpeechText }`,
given by the extension, so host tests use stand-in views (the view is W11.3's subject).
(2) Engines emit `phase`, `sttIdle` and the utterance length bound themselves (W11.1, W11.4), so
the host only forwards; it reads `utterance.tooLong?.()` for the `end` note. (3) Late frames: after
a server abort, a stream's late frames are ignored; after a normal server end only a late ABORT is;
anything else for a closed stream closes `protocol` (the contract's probe holds for the page's own
closed streams). (4) `transcribe`/`speak` on a port whose socket is not bound answer
`speechTexts.portClosed` (no text for "not yet bound"). (5) `GatewayContext.operator` is typed
optional so existing fake contexts type-check. (6) The host's `stop()` is not called by the gateway
(an extension has no unbind hook): ports close with their sockets at unbind and engines die with
the process. (8) The host never calls the process speech-out engine's `warm(options)`, so the
warm spare (D-M11-12) is not started for the shared preferences yet. (7) `test/integration/m3-gateway.test.js` l.350 pins the extras labels to
`[secretWriter, fixture]`; with the speech extension the list is `[secretWriter, fixture, speech]`,
so acceptance 16 fails until that line names `speech` (an M3 file in the core regression list).
